description:
## Why

PKIX-xj81 decomposition, pattern 3 of 6. Two trust anchors with the same
issuer/subject DN but different SPKIs. The pool builds a chain whose
terminal cert is signed by one of the two keys. The builder must pick the
right anchor (matching SPKI) and not fail just because two anchors share a DN.

## What

Pool topology:

```
TwinAnchorA  (subject="CN=Twin Root", SPKI=keyA, self-signed with keyA)
TwinAnchorB  (subject="CN=Twin Root", SPKI=keyB, self-signed with keyB)
TwinIntermediate (issuer="CN=Twin Root", signed with keyA,
                  subject="CN=Twin Intermediate", AKI=keyA-SKI)
TwinEE       (signed by TwinIntermediate)
```

Build steps:

1. Generator issues two TA certs with identical subject DN, different keys.
   Plus one intermediate signed by keyA, plus EE.
2. Test (`tests/ta_collision.rs`):
   - Anchor list: `[TwinAnchorA, TwinAnchorB]`.
   - Pool: `[TwinIntermediate]`.
   - `build_path(&ee, &pool, &anchors)` must succeed.
   - `validate_path(&chain, &anchors, ...)` must succeed and the verifier
     must accept the keyA anchor (NOT keyB) — confirm by introspecting
     anchor SPKI bytes against the path-chain[1] AKI.
3. Negative: a variant where TwinIntermediate is signed by keyA but `AKI`
   is missing. Pool builder should still find a path (tries both anchors
   and one verifies), then `validate_path` succeeds. Document this lenient
   behaviour in the test.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Four DER fixtures committed.
- [ ] Generation reproducible via `generate.sh`.
- [ ] Two integration tests: one with AKI guidance, one without.

## Depends on

PKIX-xj81.1 (shared generator + helpers).
